run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary:
All three requested counts were obtained, but two of them required using the field the indices actually map, and one is explained by the query window rather than by a clean field substitution.

1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: the requested term { level: "ERROR" } returned 0. That index has no `level` field at all; its mapping is @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword), severity (keyword). Re-running against `severity` also returned 0, and a match_all count over the whole authorized window (2026-11-20T09:03:55Z to 2026-11-21T09:03:55Z) returned total 0 with an empty severity bucket list, while the index reports docs.count = 16. So index a's ERROR count inside the authorized window is 0 because no document of that index falls inside the window, not because its entries are non-ERROR; the severity vocabulary of its 16 documents could not be read with this tool.

2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: the requested terms { level: ["ERROR","FATAL"] } returned 0; that index has no `level` field. Its severity field is the integer `severity_num`, and its documents carry [INFO]/[ERROR]/[FATAL] prefixes in `msg` with severity_num 3/5/6 respectively. terms { severity_num: [5,6] } over the authorized window returned 8, consistent with an aggregation showing severity_num 5 = 6 docs, 6 = 2 docs, 3 = 5 docs (13 docs total, all inside the window).

3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: a range filter on @timestamp plus term level ERROR returned 0 because that index maps no date field at all (fields: ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text), and the tool therefore applied no time filter. Re-running the range on `ingest_ts` for today's date (2026-11-21) with level ERROR returned 7. Error-level entries dated 2026-11-20 total 5, and a last-24-hours ingest_ts range also yields 7, so 7 holds under either reading of "today".

No fault was under investigation here; this was a log-retrieval question, so no root cause is asserted.

claims.text: Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); it has no `level` field.
The requested term { level: "ERROR" } query on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 (shards successful 1, failed 0).

On app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, term { severity: "ERROR" } over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T09:03:55Z to 2026-11-21T09:03:55Z returned total 0, and a match_all count with a terms aggregation on `severity` over the same window returned total 0 with an empty bucket list — no document of that index lies inside the authorized window.
The index listing reports app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 with docs.count 16, so the index holds 16 documents even though 0 of them matched inside the authorized window.
Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it has no `level` field.
The requested terms { level: ["ERROR","FATAL"] } query on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0.

Documents returned from app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (13 shown, timestamps 2026-11-21T09:00:01Z to 09:02:05Z, svc order-280) pair the text prefixes [INFO], [ERROR] and [FATAL] in `msg` with severity_num values 3, 5 and 6 respectively.

terms { severity_num: [5,6] } on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 over the authorized window returned total 8; the count matches the severity_num aggregation buckets of 6 docs at value 5 and 2 docs at value 6 (plus 5 docs at value 3) out of 13 total docs.
Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it maps no date field, so the search tool reported time_filter.applied = false for queries against it.

On app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, the requested bool query with range on @timestamp (2026-11-21T00:00:00 to 23:59:59) plus term level ERROR returned total 0, because @timestamp is not a field of that index.
On app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, a range on ingest_ts 2026-11-21T00:00:00 to 23:59:59 combined with term level ERROR returned total 7.

For app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the level aggregation over all 16 documents is ERROR 12 and INFO 4; the ERROR entries dated 2026-11-20 total 5 and the ingest_ts range 2026-11-20T09:03:55 to 2026-11-21T09:03:55 with level ERROR also totals 7.

The 16 documents returned from app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 show ingest_ts strings without a timezone (e.g. 2026-11-21T08:01:00, 2026-11-20T08:01:00, 2026-11-21T09:04:00) and messages such as 'err today 1', 'err yest 1' and 'info today 1'.

Use the mapped names in future queries: `severity` (keyword) on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, `severity_num` integer 5 = ERROR / 6 = FATAL (3 = INFO) on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, and `ingest_ts` (a keyword holding timezone-less ISO strings) plus `level` on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 instead of @timestamp.

If the ERROR content of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 matters, widen the readable window beyond 2026-11-20T09:03:55Z to 2026-11-21T09:03:55Z or inspect its 16 documents with a tool that does not force an @timestamp filter; within the currently authorized window its severity values cannot be listed.

gaps: Every elasticsearch_search call applies a time filter on the mapped date field that cannot be turned off; three probes of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 (default 1h window and the full authorized window) matched no documents, so the timestamps and severity values of its 16 documents fall outside the authorized window and remain unreadable here — the reported 0 for that index is a window artifact, not evidence that it contains no ERROR entries.

One app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 search that included a `source` field list returned INVALID_PARAMS with no detail, so that particular document projection was not observed; the equivalent data was obtained with an unsourced match_all and a severity aggregation instead.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-mapped field, so ingest_ts is a keyword and the date range was evaluated as a lexicographic string comparison on timezone-less values; the tool applied no time filter, and one returned document (ingest_ts 2026-11-21T09:04:00) lies after the authorized window end 2026-11-21T09:03:55Z. How those strings map to real event time (timezone) is unknown.

The literal instruction 'today' was interpreted as the UTC calendar day 2026-11-21 (the run date); the last-24-hours reading also yields 7, but a different timezone definition of today was not tested.
next_steps: Ask the index owner of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 whether its 16 documents' @timestamp values lie before or after the authorized window, and supply a window that contains them if their severity breakdown is needed.

If @timestamp-style time filtering is required on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, consider reindexing ingest_ts as a date field (with an explicit timezone) so the platform's mandatory time filter applies and counts can be tied to a window.
